Let me look at the relevant code and test.Let me see the rest of `stripFlags`, `argsMinusFirstX`, and `innerfind`.Now I understand the bug. `innerfind` uses `stripFlags` to correctly skip flag values when *finding* the subcommand name, but `argsMinusFirstX` does a naive first-match removal — so `root -f child child` removes the `-f` flag's value `child` instead of the trailing subcommand `child`, corrupting args on the recursive call.

The fix: make `argsMinusFirstX` flag-aware (mirroring `stripFlags`' logic) so it skips over flag values when searching for `x`. It needs access to the command's flag set, so it becomes a method.Target test passes. Let me run the full suite to check for regressions.Done. Full suite passes.

The bug: `innerfind` locates the next subcommand via `stripFlags`, which correctly skips flag values — but `argsMinusFirstX` then removed the *first* arg matching the subcommand name unconditionally. With `root -f child child`, it removed `-f`'s value `child` rather than the actual subcommand arg, corrupting the args on recursion.

Fix in [command.go](file:///home/andy/cogz_bench/replay_tmp/cogz_replay_6b0bd307_fmie32et/command.go): converted `argsMinusFirstX` to a `*Command` method so it can consult the flag set, and gave it the same flag-value-skipping logic as `stripFlags` — `--`/`-f` flags without `=` and without `NoOptDefVal` cause the following arg to be skipped, and `--` terminates the search. The call site now uses `c.argsMinusFirstX(innerArgs, nextSubCmd)`.
